blocks.x: This is part of Off Season Greece, a collection of guides highlighting the year-round appeal of Greece's most popular destinations, courtesy of our favorite local tastemakers. In this edition, we speak to Condé Nast Traveler's Top Travel Specialists about how to decide which off-season destination in Greece for you.

As we continue to spread the good word of traveling outside of summer—peak season for most destinations, but most of all European—let us convince you that this advice is especially prescient for Greece, which is also magical in late fall, winter (skiing, anyone?), and early spring. But you might ask, how do you even travel to Greece in the off season? This country of many island groups, from Aegean to Ionian, is not just to be experienced at its peak in the summer, when ferries are run to and fro, and your social feed becomes awash with selfies from white-plastered Mykonos. Nay—Όχι! For reasons climate- and crowd-related, certain sides of Greece shine brighter when the brutal Grecian sun lets up and Zeus’s calming clouds roll in, when you actually have breathing room at the Parthenon and can even potentially commune with Athena herself in the soft winter light of Athens. Or, hey, why not just take advantage of the cheaper hotel rates and airfare while most families are wrapped up at school? For these reasons and more, locals and in-the-know visitors know that, in Hellas, “off season” truly means “game on.”

To learn what it takes to make the most out of the off season, we tapped some of our favorite Condé Nast Traveler Top Travel Specialists who are experts on visiting Greece: Julie Durso of Scott Dunn, Lisa Kusak of Kusak & Co., Emily Rister of Original Travel, and Laura Plansky of Audley Travel. Here they tell us the pros of visiting outside of summer, where to take a city break, and what to pack so that you’re prepared for your own off-season odyssey to Greece.

Why you should visit Greece in the off season

After an entirely too-hot Eurosummer this year (every year now, it seems), the pros of visiting Greece in the cooler off season have never been more evident. “Visiting off season is perfect for avoiding crowds and the heat,” says Rister of Original Travel. “Generally, Greece can be quite mild, even in winter, so it’s still pleasant to visit and be out and about exploring. Cultural sites are much quieter and you don’t have to book restaurants weeks in advance.” Rister also says that hotel rates massively drop at this time of year, outside of the peak summer travel months, so the off season is a chance to experience luxurious properties for a fraction of the cost.

Beyond the weather and value-for-money factor, Kusak of Kusak & Co. says there’s a human element too: “In the off season you find a certain authenticity. With fewer people present, you can get a real connection with the local community—the pace is gentler for everyone.” To top it off, the off season is perhaps the best time for foodie travelers, given the bounty of the winter harvest. “The olive harvest runs from November into December, and some estates will welcome visitors to watch or take part,” Kusak explains. “Citrus season follows in the Peloponnese and Crete, when the orange and lemon groves are at their most vibrant."
